title: Wynn's European trip and Tommy Ladnier
summary: He went to Europe in October 1927 with a Spanish dance act band and worked with Tommy Ladnier.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now just a couple of minutes if you can tell about your European trip, unless there's something else you can think of too you'd like to tell about.

Well, the European trip was, it was very interesting. I enjoyed it very much. The act that, I went over to join an act that had, it was a dancing act, a Spanish act, and they had a band with them, an American band. I only knew one fellow in the band, Spallin, he was a pianist, had been with the original Jimmy Wade band. So they sent for me, in fact they sent for two of us from Chicago, they sent for Clifford King and myself. And doing the transaction, which it takes quite a bit of transaction, it did at that time from Europe. So in the meantime Clifford had, went to work with Charlie Elgar somewhere and he was doing alright, so he had been looking for us. So he backed down at the last minute. So anyway I went on over alone and joined the band. And of course I didn't know anybody in the band, but this fellow Spallin, the pianist. And after I got there there was a boy that had been here with Sammy Stewart, Roy Butler, he was on the sax and clarinet, he was with the outfit. So it was a very enjoyable trip. I worked with them for a while and the first, our first engagement, well I went directly from here to Bremen and then I had to take a train from Bremen to Hamburg, Germany. I joined them in Hamburg and they were working at a very big elaborate place. And as it would happen at the same time that I got there, Sam Wooden's band was in Hamburg, was in town and of course his band, he was this king of Europe. I mean he's the biggest thing that ever happened because he's the first one that introduced jazz all over there, he went all up in Russia and everywhere. And his name there was, he was like Paul Whiteman was over here at that time. So after the second night that I was there I went out to hear the band and of course there was two of the original members of my band, when I had my band, when I had my band here, Dreamlin in his band, it was Doc Cheatham, Adolph Cheatham, and Jerry Blake, see. And of course Tommy Ladner was in the band. Oh they had a terrific band. And when I heard that band, I mean my heart just went out for it, you know, one of those kind of things. stuff they sent me and made me offer to join the band. Well, that was right where I would want to be with my good friends, you know what I mean? And it was a terrific outfit. So I eventually went on with them and I stayed with them for the, for a period of probably three years, you know.
Is this date about right here? It's a little off.
It's about a year off all the way down. Yeah, it's about a year off all the way down.
You mean it should be a little later or earlier? A little earlier. That's the Esquire Jazz book, so we'll have it on the tape. And you were in Europe, it says here about 1929 to 31 or so.
Yeah, well that's off. I went over in 27, in October of 27. I mean, I gave this to them just from memory, but I went over in October of 27.
So those dates got to be pushed up, they're a little off. Yeah.
It's so hard. I remember those dates back.
Did you work with Tommy Ladner a while over there then?
Yeah, I did. We eventually worked together in a show over there. And we always were friends. Well, I remember Tommy from his Joe Oliver days.
